title: County purchase of land under main Kula water tank
summary: On March 21, the county moved to buy 1.811 acres in Kula for $451,561, the land under its water tank, and a member said the purchase will help maintain essential water infrastructure. The tank serves upper Kula and sits on Haleakalā Ranch land under a right-of-entry agreement. Owning it would let the Water Department make legal changes there without asking the ranch.

timeline.text: A member said buying the land under the county water tank will help maintain essential water infrastructure.
The county built the water tank on Haleakalā Ranch's property and has run it under a right-of-entry agreement.
The county is buying 1.811 acres for $451,561.
The resolution goes to the full council for its consideration.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The committee voted 7–0 to send the amended resolution to the full council.

timeline.text: The committee voted 7–0 to replace the resolution with a revised draft.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The revised draft confirms appraised values of $450,000 for the land and $1,561 for the easement.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The department said the tank sits on Haleakalā Ranch land through the ranch's kindness, with no sale yet.

timeline.text: The Water Department said the land holds the main water tank for upper Kula residents.
